name: Electric Bicycle
description: A bicycle or tricycle with fully operable pedals and an electric motor of 750 watts or less, in one of two classes: pedal assist to 20 mph, or throttle to 20 mph. Massachusetts recognizes no Class 3.

restrictions.rule: A bicycle or tricycle with fully operable pedals and an electric motor of 750 watts or less (Massachusetts General Laws chapter 90 §1)
Class 1: pedal assist only, ceasing at 20 mph; Class 2: may be propelled by the motor alone, with no assistance above 20 mph (Massachusetts General Laws chapter 90 §1)

No Class 3: one that assists past 20 mph isn't an electric bicycle, and may instead fall under motorized bicycle rules (driver's license, helmet, riders 16 or older, 25 mph cap, kept off off-street bike paths) (Massachusetts General Laws chapter 90 §1)
Riders and passengers 16 or younger must wear a CPSC-compliant bicycle helmet
Manufacturers must permanently affix a label stating its class, top assisted speed and motor wattage (Massachusetts General Laws chapter 85 §11B¾)
Must not be modified to change its motor-powered speed or engagement unless the label is replaced to match (Massachusetts General Laws chapter 85 §11B¾)
Meets the CPSC's bicycle requirements (Massachusetts General Laws chapter 85 §11B¾)
Has the rights and duties of a bicycle and is not a motor vehicle or motorized bicycle: no driver's license or registration (Massachusetts General Laws chapter 85 §11B¾ and chapter 90 §1)
May use all public ways except limited-access highways posted against bicycles, and bike lanes
Never ridden on sidewalks, unlike a conventional bicycle (Massachusetts General Laws chapter 85 §11B¾)

A municipality or state agency may ban or regulate it, including with speed limits, on a bike path or bikeway it manages, but only after public notice and a hearing (Massachusetts General Laws chapter 85 §11B¾)
Barred from nonmotorized natural-surface trails unless the agency that manages the trail allows it after public notice and a hearing (Massachusetts General Laws chapter 85 §11B¾)

On DCR land, Class 1 may use improved trails at least 8 feet wide; Class 2 is limited to places open to vehicles and bike lanes on DCR roads, and no e-bike may use a natural-surface trail (302 CMR 12.12)
